figures.caption: Figure 1 Overview of the ARCTIC system. Data sources (left) feed into three layers: the Forest View infers developer intent and detects drift via backtranslation; the Trees View ranks code regions by review-worthiness; and the Foundation provides a taxonomy-guided prioritization based on 18K human code reviews. Outputs (right) combine into a unified reviewer experience supporting self-review and directed peer review.
Table 8 Adoption and guardrail metrics from the progressive rollout of the self-review experience powered by ARCTIC signals.

Figure 2 The ARCTIC Code Critique interface (mocked-up for a fictional diff adding retry logic, +892 lines). The top row shows Intent Summary (RQ3): goals extracted from the developer/AI conversation; Intent Drift (RQ4): a scored assessment of which goals were satisfied; and Code Spotlight (RQ5): the top regions ranked by review priority. Key Milestones below summarize the agent’s trajectory steps.

Table 3 RQ3 Results. Comparison of agentic and zero-shot intent prediction across 121 AI-generated diffs. The agentic approach achieves higher F1 and precision while maintaining comparable recall, at roughly 2.3x the latency and 6.4x the token usage.
